conversation: Good to see everyone. My family taught me to fish here, and I want this lake to keep supporting our village. With 100 tons in the lake, we can each catch 10 tons this month and leave 50 to double back to 100. That’s $10,000 apiece each month if we stick to it. Can we agree to that limit and check our catches together each month? John, what do you think?

I’m in, Luke—10 tons for me. My family has depended on this lake for years, and I want our village’s children to have that same chance. Let’s make 50 tons our total limit, not a target to exceed if someone catches less. We can review the stock and everyone’s catches each month. John, does that work for you?

Count me in for 10 tons. I learned to fish here with my family, and keeping the lake healthy matters more than one big payday. If the stock ever falls below 100 tons, let’s agree on smaller catches before we fish so we leave enough for recovery. John, can you commit to the limit too?

I’m committed to 10 tons this month. My family taught me to make a living from this lake without taking away tomorrow’s catch. I also agree we should reduce our limits together if the stock drops and review everyone’s catches each month. Jack, are you willing to join us on those terms?

I’m in—10 tons for me this month, with 50 tons left in the lake to replenish. This lake is our shared livelihood, and I want it to keep supporting the village. We’ve all agreed, so let’s stick to our limits and meet again after the catches are reported to check the stock and plan next month.
